clue.text: Old as a voracious vampire

definitions.meaning: read literally: a hungry vampire is yearning in its fangs, longing in the tooth

explanation.surface: An aged bloodsucker is described as greedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means elderly (from horses' gums receding with age); the second reading splits it as a vampire's appetite felt in the teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone ageing, as horses' teeth look longer when gums recede; a hungry vampire's craving would be felt at its fangs.

clue.text: Fertiliser can put up the price

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word for can is written bottom to top

parts.note: a can is a tin
a price is a rate charged

explanation.surface: Fertiliser might raise what a farmer pays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns TIN into NIT; 'can' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates are salts widely spread on fields as a fertiliser supplying nitrogen.

clue.text: To some extent Spain caused his demise

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Spain was partly responsible for a man's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: the man whose demise Spain caused was a member of the Andean empire conquered by Spanish conquistadors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish conquest under Pizarro brought down the Andean empire and its ruler Atahualpa, whose people this word names.

clue.text: Contracting to record Wagnerian operas

parts.note: to record something is to tape it
Wagner's Ring cycle is a set of four operas

explanation.surface: Someone is signing a deal to record Wagner's operas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracting' suggests signing contracts, but it means narrowing. The Ring is Wagner's four-opera cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something narrowing gradually towards a point is getting smaller, i.e. contracting.

clue.text: Offer from former nurse

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: A proposal comes from a one-time nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out a hand or an invitation is to offer it.

clue.text: Enid let boy run wild, as ordered

indicators.note: running wild means behaving without order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A mother named Enid allows her son to run wild, as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run wild' rearranges ENIDLETBOY; the surface irony is that the definition is the opposite of running wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something dutifully in compliance with instructions is doing it as ordered.

clue.text: Foot of a fabulous bird in the Egyptian enclosure

indicators.note: the bird is placed in the words that follow, which enclose it

parts.note: taken as written
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend
E is an abbreviation for Egyptian, as on currency

explanation.surface: The claw of a mythical bird is kept in an Egyptian pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ROC inside THE + E, after the T; 'enclosure' only reinforces the containment. 'Foot' is the metrical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a metrical unit of a long syllable then a short one is this kind of foot.

clue.text: Miner agreed to be rehabilitated by European police

indicators.note: rehabilitation remakes something, so these letters are reformed into a new order

explanation.surface: A miner consents to rehabilitation run by European police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be rehabilitated' rearranges MINERAGREED; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The French national police force, a military body, is the gendarmerie.

clue.text: Vessel in which to pile grass

parts.note: to pile up goods is to stock them
grass is slang for cannabis, also called pot

explanation.surface: A container for heaping up cut grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' means cannabis, POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep cooking pan for simmering soup bases is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Lyric poem is drawn from a series of incidents

indicators.note: drawn from means taken out of, so these two letters are removed

parts.note: an episode is a series of incidents forming one part of a story
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poem is based on a sequence of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn from' looks like 'derived from' but signals removal of IS from EPISODE.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical verse it is an ode form in which a long line is followed by a shorter one.

clue.text: A fellow supporting Eastern country in property negotiations

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece supporting another sits below it

parts.note: a state is a country
a gent is a fellow, a man

explanation.surface: A man backs an Eastern nation during talks over territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts A GENT under E STATE in the down grid; the definition is descriptive, the person found in property negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who sells houses on clients' behalf haggles over prices between buyer and seller.

clue.text: Moves the camera round to take a shot

indicators.note: turning round means the word is written backwards

parts.note: a camera operator pans by swinging the camera horizontally

explanation.surface: A photographer swings the camera to take a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns PANS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a quick photograph is snapping it.

clue.text: High-fibre cereal served up with a flourish!

definitions.note: the definition describes something that has been waved about with a flourish

parts.note: bran is the fibrous husk of grain eaten as a cereal
food served up is dished

explanation.surface: Breakfast cereal is presented with great showmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer describes something waved with a flourish, as a sword is.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon flourished or waved theatrically has been brandished.

clue.text: The last 'in children's curriculum

parts.note: the three Rs of schooling are reading, 'riting and a third subject, the last of them, also spoken with its first letters dropped

explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and 'rithmetic; the apostrophe mimics the dropped letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sums with numbers are the third of the basic skills taught in primary school.

clue.text: But in Germany bombastic talk is not typical

parts.note: aber is the German word for but
a rant is loud, bombastic talk

explanation.surface: Yet ranting in Germany is said to be unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Deviating from what is normal or expected is the opposite of typical.

clue.text: Aim by each monarch to win affection

parts.note: an end is an aim, a goal
R is short for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: Every king's goal is to be loved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To make oneself beloved by others is to gain their fondness.

clue.text: Blue pencil for one in a Delaware school

parts.note: Del is the abbreviation for the US state of Delaware

indicators.note: the number goes inside the school's name

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A blue pencil is used as an example in an American school.
explanation.walkthrough: To blue-pencil a text is to cut it, from editors' blue pencils. 'for' is a link; 'one' looks like part of 'for one' but gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor's cut, made in blue pencil, is a removal of text.

clue.text: Spent a couple of notes before the bazaar

indicators.note: one piece comes before the other in the answer

parts.note: E and F are two musical notes
a fete is an outdoor fund-raising bazaar

explanation.surface: Someone spent a few banknotes before going to the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests money but means musical notes. A fete is a British village fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted or worn out, having lost vigour, is a meaning of spent.

clue.text: Charge made by soldiers in battle

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed inside the word for battle

parts.note: a battle is a fight
RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers

explanation.surface: A cavalry charge is made by troops in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests an attack but is a fee for carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment for transporting goods, the cost of carriage, is a charge.

clue.text: Good show! You and I are going to tour Teeside

parts.words: You and I are going to
parts.note: we'll, written without its apostrophe, means you and I will
to do a city is to tour its sights
Teesside is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: Bravo! The two of us will visit the Tees valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Teesside is the area around the river Tees in north-east England, abbreviated NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of congratulation on a fine performance.

clue.text: Old Latvian city note for Japanese art

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An ancient Baltic city's note is exchanged for Japanese artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper folding into figures is a traditional craft from Japan.

clue.text: The way Ernest acquires a lot of bones

indicators.note: one name acquires a letter added at its end

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
Ern is a familiar short form of the name Ernest

explanation.surface: This is how Ernest comes into possession of many bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' signals a plural: the answer is the plural of the breastbone's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone is the sternum, and several of them make a plural set of bones.

clue.text: An undefined issue requires intelligence

definitions.meaning: a vague matter in a grey area, neither black nor white
brains, the tissue of the brain standing for cleverness

explanation.surface: A vague problem calls for brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey brain tissue stands for brainpower, while a matter in a grey area is an unclear issue.

clue.text: Back in one minute, little one

indicators.note: back means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone promises to return in a moment, little one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in one minute' reads as a note on a door, but 'Back' turns IN + I + M into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small car or a short skirt is a little one of its kind.

clue.text: Small gash in the tail

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing
a gash is a cut

explanation.surface: A small wound appears on an animal's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer is called this.

clue.text: Nearly time-time for bed

parts.note: nigh means near or nearly

explanation.surface: It's almost bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours are when people go to sleep.

clue.text: Mac scrambled into a car

indicators.note: scrambling mixes things up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone named Mac clambered into a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' rearranges INTOACAR; 'Mac' looks like a name but is a mackintosh.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh, or mac, is a waterproof coat.

clue.text: Never persevered? No, quite the opposite!

definitions.text: Never persevered? No, quite the opposite!

parts.words: Never persevered? No, quite the opposite!
parts.note: read literally, the phrase seems to say someone stuck at no task, yet the idiom describes someone ruthless who will do anything

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means would go to any lengths, the reverse of its literal reading as never persisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ruthless, prepared to do anything however wicked, is said to have this attitude.
